newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches to be played in the English premier league this weekend (league positions in parentheses; all kick-off times GMT):

Leeds manager George Graham returns to Highbury where he won six major trophies in eight years before his dismissal last year. His Leeds team are looking for only their second league win in eight matches.

The death of Chelsea's vice-chairman Matthew Harding will overshadow the match between these London rivals both searching for some consistency. Spurs have revived recently and will be looking for their fourth successive win.

Liam Daish returns to Coventry's defence after suspension and will take the place of injured Paul Williams. Wednesday won their opening four matches of the season but have now gone eight games without a win.
League leaders Newcastle will be without striker Alan Shearer following his groin operation. Colombian Faustino Asprilla is likely to start in his place.
Wimbledon go to erratic Middlesbrough looking for their eighth successive league win, with Bryan Robson's side having faded after a bright start.

Southampton will be without injured skipper Barry Venison and defender Ken Monkou against a United side anxious to avoid a repeat of their defeat here last season which they claimed was the result of wearing grey shirts.

Sunderland, beaten by a last-minute goal at Tottenham in the League Cup on Wednesday, have been playing well but have gone four games without a win. Villa have trouble scoring and could struggle again against French goalkeeper Lionel Perez, who was outstanding against Tottenham.

Rovers go to Upton Park managerless after the resignation of Ray Harford and bottom of the table without a win. West Ham, inspired by Portuguese schemer Hugo Porfirio, should ensure their misery continues.
Last time these teams met in the league in 1991, Liverpool won 7-1. A similar scoreline is doubtful, but Liverpool should pick up all three points.
Forest are in a slump, without a league win since the opening day of the season. Everton have won their last two matches but are yet to win away and may have to settle for draw.
